title: Expressionism: Munch and The Scream
subject: art
description: Expressionism gives priority to inner emotion over the outer world. With **Munch** and *The Scream*, modern angst becomes an icon.

hero.hook: A cry without sound, a sky that screams: the face of modern anguish.

blocks.text: **expressionism** flourished between **1880** and **1930**. Where Impressionism captured the light of the external world, this movement projects interiority onto reality. It distorts, forces the colors, hardens the line.
The Norwegian **Edvard Munch** is a pioneer. With *The Scream*, the anguish and loneliness of modern man become a universal symbol.

sections.title: Distort to tell the true feeling

blocks.text: Europe is industrializing. Many artists feel a  about the city. Against the , who believes he explains everything through science, they make painting the territory of the . [[disenchantment]] [[positivism]] [[subjectivity]]

No more *mimesis*, the faithful imitation of nature. Colors no longer copy reality: they carry a symbolic value. In Germany, two groups structure breathing: , more raw and instinctive, and , more spiritual and oriented towards abstraction. Van Gogh and Gauguin had already paved the way. [[Die Brücke]] [[Der Blaue Reiter]]
The word “expressionism” was first used, in 1911 at the Berlin Secession, to distinguish artists who refused impressionist gentleness.
In Munch, the lines of the landscape seem to suck in the characters. Deformation is no longer a clumsiness: it is a strategy for painting the  and the raw feeling. [[nothingness]]

Munch's work is marked by early bereavements. In a pious and fragile family, he lost his mother and his sister Sophie to tuberculosis. Painting becomes a necessity: fixing the terrors so as not to be consumed by them.

blocks.caption: The Oslo Fjord: the real landscape behind the Scream's vision.

blocks.text: Munch often slept with the lights on, believing that the spirits of his deceased family visited him at night.

The origin of *Cry* dates back to a walk on  hill in Oslo. The sunset sky becomes a fire. Some link this vision to the : the ashes of the volcano had tinted the sunsets blood red all over the world. For Munch, it's no longer the weather: it's the cosmos that screams. [[Ekeberg]] [[Eruption of Krakatoa (1883) and the red sky]]

The first version of *Cry* dates from **1893**. It is part of “The Frieze of Life”, where Munch explores love, anguish and death. He paints **oven versions** (tempera, pastel, oil): the motif haunts him.

blocks.caption: The Scream: the figure covers its ears against the howl of the world.

blocks.text: A pencil inscription on the 1893 version reads: “Can only have been painted by a madman.” Infrared imagery proved in 2021 that it was Munch himself who wrote it.

The spectral figure is reminiscent of a mummy. His hands cover his ears: the cry is internal. The bridge with its rigid lines evokes civilization; the curves of the sky, a monstrous nature. Stolen from the  as well as from the Munch Museum, the painting gained the aura of a “cursed” painting. [[Oslo National Gallery]]

sections.title: From intimate trauma to global icon

blocks.text: *The Scream* has overtaken Munch. Horror cinema, parodies, derivative products: existential anxiety has become a shared language. By daring the “ugliness” of the face disfigured by fear, Munch proved that psychological truth matters more than perfect anatomy.

blocks.text: This audacity opens the way to  and contemporary art. Giving form to an inaudible cry: this is the collective catharsis of expressionism. [[surrealism]]
Born from Munch's traumas, expressionism distorts reality through color and line. With *The Scream*, personal anguish becomes the universal icon of modernity.
